title: Configuring Emergency Access: availability, settings, authentication domains, Microtenants

prose.text: Setting up the feature is a gate, then identity, then the Emergency Access page. {{limited-availability}} {{purpose}}

prose.label: Settings.
prose.text: {{settings}} The IdP and token requirements are in [[zpa.emergency-access.identity]].

prose.label: Authentication domains.
prose.text: {{domains-semantics}} {{domain-removal}} How to take back an approval whose domain was removed is open {{gap:approval-removal-paths}}.

prose.label: Microtenants.
prose.text: {{microtenant-rules}} {{microtenant-privileged-approvals}} The two do not obviously fit together {{divergence:microtenant-user-access}}.
The users page and statuses: [[zpa.emergency-access.users]]. What the feature covers and does not: [[zpa.emergency-access.scope]].

checks.do: Whether the feature has been enabled by Zscaler Support, since the page does not exist otherwise.
Whether the tenant is the Default Microtenant, and whether the Microtenant has Privileged Approvals enabled.
The Emergency Authentication Domains list against the domain used on a privileged approval.

limited-availability.statement: Emergency Access is in limited availability, and Zscaler Support enables it for an organization.

quotes: This feature and its procedures are in limited availability. Contact Zscaler Support to enable this feature for your organization.

purpose.statement: Emergency access provisions third-party users such as contractors and vendors for access to time-bound resources, and builds on the IdPs available in Private Access with arbitrary authentication domains.

quotes: You can provision third-party users (e.g., contractors and vendors) for emergency access to time-bound resources. Emergency access builds on top of identity providers (IdPs) that are available in Private Access (ZPA), along with arbitrary authentication domains

create-with-approval.statement: A user designated for emergency access is created within the emergency access IdP when a privileged approval is created for that user.

quotes: You can create a user designated for emergency access within the IdP enabled for emergency access when creating a privileged approval for that user.

settings.statement: The Emergency Access page has an IdP (read-only), an IdP API Token, a User Group Name where new users are created, and Emergency Authentication Domains.

quotes: IdP: The IdP that has Use with Arbitrary Domains enabled. This is a read-only field.
**User Group Name**: The name of the user group where the new users are created.
evidence.after: For Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service

quotes: **IdP API Token**: Enter the Okta API token with the necessary group administrator permissions for the group that will be designated for emergency access, but is not yet created.
Emergency Authentication Domains: (Optional) Enter the email address domains to manage or limit the user authentication domains for emergency access when creating privileged approvals
evidence.after: For Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service

domains-semantics.statement: If Emergency Authentication Domains are set, only those email domains can be used when adding a privileged approval; if none are set, users can be created from any authentication domain that is not an existing primary or secondary authentication domain.

quotes: If added, only the email address domain configured in the **Emergency Authentication Domains** field can be used when adding a privileged approval. When no authentication domains are specified, users can be created from any authentication domain that is not an existing primary or secondary authentication domain.
evidence.after: For Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service

domain-removal.statement: Removing an email domain from the Emergency Authentication Domains field does not remove the privileged approvals created with it.

quotes: If an existing email address domain is removed from the **Emergency Authentication Domain** field, the privileged approvals created with it continue to be present.
evidence.after: For Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service

microtenant-rules.statement: Within a Microtenant, only the Default Microtenant can configure emergency access, and Microtenants with Privileged Approvals disabled can still create or edit emergency access users.

quotes: Only the Default Microtenant can configure emergency access.
Emergency access users can be created or edited by Microtenants that have Privileged Approvals disabled.

microtenant-privileged-approvals.statement: The Emergency Access and Emergency Access Users pages are not visible for Microtenants with Privileged Approvals disabled, the default for that Microtenant field.

quotes: The Emergency Access and Emergency Access Users pages are not visible for Microtenants with **Privileged Approvals** disabled. This field is **Disabled** by default.
The Emergency Access Users page is not visible if you are within a Microtenant that has Privileged Approvals disabled.

approval-removal-paths.title: How an approval created with a removed domain is ended
approval-removal-paths.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Privileged approvals created with a domain that is subsequently removed ... remain active. Expiry or manual deactivation is the only removal path." The help says the approvals continue to be present. The privileged-approval article says approvals expire when their window ends; manual deactivation of an approval is not described in the captures.

microtenant-user-access.summary: Microtenants with Privileged Approvals disabled can create or edit emergency access users, yet the Emergency Access Users page is not visible to them.

quotes: Emergency access users can be created or edited by Microtenants that have Privileged Approvals disabled.

positions.says: Emergency access users can be created or edited by Microtenants that have Privileged Approvals disabled.

quotes: The Emergency Access Users page is not visible if you are within a Microtenant that has Privileged Approvals disabled.

positions.says: The Emergency Access Users page is not visible within a Microtenant that has Privileged Approvals disabled.

microtenant-user-access.impact: It is not stated how such a Microtenant creates or edits users without the page (possibly by API or from the Default Microtenant). Do not tell an admin in that Microtenant to use the page.
